---
name: observability
description: Design, add, or review operational instrumentation that makes running systems diagnosable.
---

# Observability

Make the affected behavior understandable from signals available to a person or
agent arriving without the original context. Preserve the requested scope: design
and review produce recommendations; authorized implementation adds and verifies
the instrumentation. Work with the project's existing language and telemetry tools.

## Establish the diagnostic questions

Read the affected operations, entry points, asynchronous boundaries, failure paths,
and existing logs, metrics, traces, status surfaces and alerts. Identify who uses
the signals, where they can read them, and the relevant access, retention and cost
constraints. Reuse useful coverage before adding another producer or backend.

Choose concrete questions from the task and plausible failure modes: which run
failed, why a branch was taken, whether work is progressing, how often a dependency
fails, or where time is spent. Map each question to the smallest useful signal and
an observation that would answer it. Include success or recovery when needed to
distinguish failure from expected operation. A simple change need not acquire every
signal type, a dashboard, an alert or a new service.

`debug` owns investigating an observed failure; this skill owns durable diagnostic
coverage. `error-handling` owns caller-visible errors, retries and recovery policy.
An instrumentation change preserves results, exceptions, cancellation, effects and
retry ownership unless a behavior change is also authorized. Report a swallowed
failure rather than silently redesigning its public contract to expose it.

## Instrument the deciding boundaries

Use established event names, levels, units and semantic conventions. Record
meaningful outcomes and decisions, including the safe values or classifications
that explain them. Function entry/exit chatter rarely answers an operational
question. Give duplicate reports of one failure a clear owner rather than paging
at every layer.

| Signal | Use it to answer | Preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Structured log or event | What happened in this particular operation, and why? | Stable event name, time, operation/run identity, outcome and useful decision context |
| Metric | How much, how often, how slow, or how saturated? | Defined units, counted population, time window and bounded dimensions; distinguish attempts from logical operations |
| Trace | Where did an operation spend time across components? | The existing trace context, meaningful spans and links across synchronous and asynchronous boundaries |
| Health or status surface | Is a process alive, ready or making progress? | The specific state being measured, its scope and freshness; absence of errors alone is not evidence of health |

Create or validate correlation context at the trusted entry point and propagate it
through the affected calls, queues and workers. When several entry points share a
sink, record which entry point started the work alongside its run identity; a
correlation ID alone cannot establish that. Keep retries and child operations
associated without conflating separate executions. Treat incoming identifiers as
untrusted, bounded input and use the existing propagation format.

For metrics, use a bounded vocabulary such as operation, route template or outcome
class. Request IDs, user IDs, raw URLs and arbitrary error text do not belong in
metric dimensions. Histograms or an existing distribution measure support tail
latency questions; an average alone does not. Confirm what the instrument counts,
including retries, partial results and zero traffic, before deriving a rate.

Reuse existing tracing and auto-instrumentation; add manual spans where they answer
a missing question. Choose sampling and retention against diagnostic needs and
cost. Sampled traces cannot establish complete event counts or that an unrecorded
failure never happened. OpenTelemetry is an option, not a required migration.

## Keep diagnostic data safe and affordable

Allowlist fields before emission to logs, spans, metrics, persisted failures and
status responses. Raw exception messages, causes, stacks, URLs and payloads can
contain secrets or personal data even when the public error is generic. Preserve
useful classification and safe identifiers without copying unrestricted objects.
Apply the project's access and retention policy to every new diagnostic surface.

Bound payload size, label cardinality, event volume and buffer growth. Avoid
expensive serialization, blocking writes or per-iteration logging on hot paths;
aggregate, sample or use existing buffering when appropriate. Account for exporter
failure and backpressure so added telemetry does not unexpectedly fail or stall
the operation. Preserve an established mandatory audit contract, including its
failure policy, rather than silently making it best effort.

## Preserve evidence for unattended work

For background jobs, watchers or long-running processes, identify what remains
available after a crash or restart. Use the existing durable sink or state store;
add a failure record only where the diagnostic question needs one. Include safe
operation identity, phase, time, attempt and failure classification.

Scope state to the run or work item that produced it. Use the storage mechanism's
atomicity and concurrency controls so concurrent writers or a partial write do
not destroy evidence. Distinguish historical failure from current state: define
freshness and how success, recovery, restart or expiration updates it. An unrelated
successful job must not erase another job's failure.

Keep status reads cheap and free of business side effects. Distinguish liveness,
readiness and progress using the project's existing contract; a dependency outage
does not automatically justify declaring the process dead and restarting it.
Expose only the detail the intended reader is authorized to see.

## Add actionable alerts when needed

Use existing alert ownership, severity and delivery conventions. Choose conditions
that justify an action, usually user-visible errors, latency or delayed work; a
resource signal is useful when it predicts a concrete operational consequence.
Derive thresholds, duration and recovery conditions from service objectives,
observed behavior or an explicit project requirement. Identify the responder and
link the first useful query, mitigation or runbook. State how no traffic, stale
data and missing telemetry differ from recovery. Do not invent universal numbers
or delete existing alerts merely because they use another convention.

## Verify the signals at their destination

Exercise the affected success and representative failure paths within an isolated,
authorized environment. Confirm that the intended trigger actually occurred, then
read the resulting events, metric series, traces or status at the consumer. Check
correlation across relevant entry points and boundaries, safe fields, expected
counts and units, and any new state lifecycle. A configured exporter or successful
test command alone does not prove that a signal arrived.

Use test collectors and notification sinks for failure injection and alert tests.
Production disruption, threshold changes or messages to real recipients need
authority from the active task; this skill grants none. Test delivery only through
the stages actually available and report unavailable destinations separately.
Missing or sampled-away data is unknown, not a zero error rate or verified health.

Verify that instrumentation preserves functional outcomes and relevant failure
behavior; exercise a telemetry outage when its new failure path can affect them.
Measure overhead under representative conditions when the changed path or budget
makes it material. Use available `verify` and project checks for execution evidence;
direct checks remain useful when that skill is unavailable. Remove only temporary
probes and fault controls owned by the task, preserving useful diagnostic evidence.

Report the questions covered, changes or findings, where and how to inspect each
signal, observed checks and remaining blind spots. Keep implementation, tested
delivery and production operation distinct. Return to the active caller for
remaining work; `ci-cd-automation` owns rollout gates and recovery, and publication
or ongoing monitoring follows the user's existing scope.

import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from runner import ProviderError, Runner
from telemetry import Telemetry


class Provider:
    def __init__(self, error=None):
        self.error = error
        self.calls = []

    def send(self, job):
        self.calls.append(job)
        if self.error:
            raise self.error
        return "receipt-12"


class ContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_success_after_fresh_worker_start(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            provider = Provider()
            telemetry = Telemetry(root / "signals")
            producer = Runner(root / "queue", provider, telemetry)
            job = {"kind": "invoice", "email": "private@example.test", "credential": "fixture-only-token"}
            run_id = producer.scheduled(job)
            consumer = Runner(root / "queue", provider, telemetry)

            result = consumer.execute(run_id)

            self.assertEqual(result, {"run_id": run_id, "ok": True, "receipt": "receipt-12"})
            self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [job])
            self.assertFalse((root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).exists())

    def test_provider_failure_keeps_result_and_at_most_once_attempt(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            error = ProviderError("TIMEOUT", "Authorization=fixture-only-token; email=private@example.test")
            provider = Provider(error)
            runner = Runner(root / "queue", provider, Telemetry(root / "signals"))
            job = {"kind": "invoice", "email": "private@example.test", "credential": "fixture-only-token"}
            run_id = runner.manual(job)

            result = runner.execute(run_id)

            self.assertEqual(result, {"run_id": run_id, "ok": False, "code": "TIMEOUT"})
            self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [job])
            self.assertFalse((root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).exists())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

OBSERVABILITY.md.content:
# Local batch-run signals

`scheduled()` and `manual()` persist their entry point in the private queue
message. A new worker reads it without requiring the producer's process or
telemetry. Older messages and unrecognized values use `unknown`. The initial
`load` signal also uses `unknown` until the queue message has been read.

The existing local collector writes three views:

- `events.jsonl`: `batch_run` events with `run_id`, `entrypoint`, `stage` and
  `status`. Filter by `run_id` to follow a run across producer and worker.
- `run-<run_id>.json`: the latest observed stage and status for that run. Stages
  are `enqueue`, `queued`, `load`, `send`, `acknowledge` and `complete`. A failed
  state also has `failure_kind` and `failure_stage`. A handled provider error
  finishes at `complete` with status `failed` and failure stage `send`, after the
  queue message has been consumed.
- `metrics.jsonl`: `batch_runs_queued` and `batch_enqueue_failures`, labeled by
  entry point, plus `batch_run_outcomes`, labeled by entry point and outcome
  (`success`, `provider_error` or `unexpected_error`). Each returning or raising
  execution attempts one outcome increment. The collector adds timestamps.

To compare execution failure rates, use matching time windows and entry points:
sum the outcome amounts for `provider_error` and `unexpected_error`, then divide
by the amounts for all three outcomes. A window with no outcomes has no rate.
These are execution-attempt counts, not deduplicated unique-run counts. Enqueue
failures are separate because no worker execution has started.

An unexpected exception records its current stage and is re-raised unchanged.
The existing queue retention and provider-call behavior remain in place. A state
left at `send`/`running` establishes only the last observed stage. It does not
prove that a worker crashed or that the provider failed; an interrupted worker
may leave no terminal event or outcome increment.

Signals omit job fields, provider diagnostics, raw provider error codes and
receipts. Run IDs appear in events and per-run state, never in metric labels.
The label values are bounded by the application.

Collector operations are independent and best effort. An unavailable surface
does not suppress attempts to use the other surfaces or change business results.
Signals can be missing or disagree, and a state file can be stale. There is no
atomic transaction between queue changes and signals, telemetry retry, guaranteed
delivery, retention policy or alert notification. Tests exercise only the supplied
local file collector; they establish no external backend or notification delivery.

PROJECT.md.content:
# Batch sender

The scheduler and manual operator enqueue work; another Runner instance executes
it after the producer has exited. A known ProviderError is returned as an outcome
and consumes the message. The external provider is called once per execution.
Other exceptions retain their existing behavior. This exercise has no live service.

telemetry.py is the existing local collector, not a mandatory audit trail. It
records exactly the fields supplied; it does not redact them. Its event, counter
and per-key state APIs write real files. New instrumentation can use these APIs.
The collector can be unavailable. The queue payload is private application state;
signals are read by support staff. Customer fields and provider diagnostics in the
fixtures are synthetic but represent confidential production data.

Public methods and result shapes are established contracts. No new backend,
package, deployment, notification channel or retry policy is requested.
Run the existing contract tests with python3 -m unittest -v. Add meaningful checks
for new instrumentation when needed.

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

from runner import ProviderError, Runner
from telemetry import Telemetry
from test_runner import Provider


class ObservabilityTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        folder = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=Path(__file__).parent)
        self.addCleanup(folder.cleanup)
        self.root = Path(folder.name)
        self.telemetry = Telemetry(self.root / "signals")
        self.job = {
            "kind": "private-invoice-kind",
            "email": "private@example.test",
            "credential": "fixture-only-token",
        }

    def runner(self, provider=None, telemetry=None):
        return Runner(self.root / "queue", provider or Provider(), telemetry or self.telemetry)

    def records(self, filename):
        path = self.root / "signals" / filename
        return [json.loads(line) for line in path.read_text().splitlines()] if path.exists() else []

    def state(self, run_id):
        return json.loads((self.root / "signals" / ("run-" + run_id + ".json")).read_text())

    def outcomes(self):
        return [row for row in self.records("metrics.jsonl") if row["metric"] == "batch_run_outcomes"]

    def assert_private_signals(self, *extra_values):
        contents = "\n".join(path.read_text() for path in (self.root / "signals").iterdir())
        for value in [*self.job.values(), "receipt-12", *extra_values]:
            self.assertNotIn(value, contents)
        for row in self.records("metrics.jsonl"):
            self.assertLessEqual(set(row["labels"]), {"entrypoint", "outcome"})
            self.assertIn(row["labels"]["entrypoint"], {"scheduled", "manual", "unknown"})
            if "outcome" in row["labels"]:
                self.assertIn(row["labels"]["outcome"], {"success", "provider_error", "unexpected_error"})

    def test_entrypoint_survives_producer_exit_without_producer_signals(self):
        script = """
import sys
from runner import Runner
from telemetry import Telemetry
producer = Runner(sys.argv[1] + '/queue', object(), Telemetry(sys.argv[1] + '/signals', available=False))
print(getattr(producer, sys.argv[2])({'kind': 'private-invoice-kind', 'email': 'private@example.test', 'credential': 'fixture-only-token'}))
"""
        for entrypoint in ("scheduled", "manual"):
            with self.subTest(entrypoint=entrypoint):
                producer = subprocess.run(
                    [sys.executable, "-c", script, str(self.root), entrypoint],
                    cwd=Path(__file__).parent,
                    env={**os.environ, "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1"},
                    capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, timeout=10,
                )
                run_id = producer.stdout.strip()
                provider = Provider()

                result = self.runner(provider).execute(run_id)

                self.assertEqual(result, {"run_id": run_id, "ok": True, "receipt": "receipt-12"})
                self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [self.job])
                self.assertEqual(self.state(run_id)["entrypoint"], entrypoint)
                self.assertEqual(self.state(run_id)["status"], "succeeded")
                self.assertEqual(self.state(run_id)["stage"], "complete")
                self.assertFalse((self.root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).exists())
                events = [row for row in self.records("events.jsonl") if row["run_id"] == run_id]
                self.assertEqual(events[0]["stage"], "load")
                self.assertTrue(all(row["entrypoint"] == entrypoint for row in events[1:]))
        self.assertEqual(len(self.outcomes()), 2)
        self.assert_private_signals()

    def test_queued_and_inflight_state_are_visible_before_completion(self):
        runner = self.runner()
        run_id = runner.scheduled(self.job)
        queued = self.state(run_id)

        def inspect_inflight(job):
            state = self.state(run_id)
            self.assertEqual((state["stage"], state["status"]), ("send", "running"))
            self.assertEqual(state["entrypoint"], "scheduled")
            self.assertEqual(job, self.job)
            raise KeyboardInterrupt()

        runner.provider.send = inspect_inflight
        with self.assertRaises(KeyboardInterrupt):
            runner.execute(run_id)

        self.assertEqual((queued["stage"], queued["status"]), ("queued", "queued"))
        self.assertEqual(self.state(run_id)["stage"], "send")
        self.assertEqual(self.state(run_id)["status"], "running")
        self.assertTrue((self.root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).exists())
        self.assertEqual(self.outcomes(), [])

    def test_provider_failure_is_counted_once_after_consuming_message(self):
        code = "CUSTOMER-private@example.test-fixture-only-token"
        provider = Provider(ProviderError(code, "Authorization=fixture-only-token"))
        runner = self.runner(provider)
        run_id = runner.manual(self.job)

        result = self.runner(provider).execute(run_id)

        self.assertEqual(result, {"run_id": run_id, "ok": False, "code": code})
        self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [self.job])
        self.assertFalse((self.root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).exists())
        state = self.state(run_id)
        self.assertEqual((state["stage"], state["status"]), ("complete", "failed"))
        self.assertEqual((state["failure_stage"], state["failure_kind"]), ("send", "provider_error"))
        outcomes = self.outcomes()
        self.assertEqual(len(outcomes), 1)
        self.assertEqual(outcomes[0]["amount"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(outcomes[0]["labels"], {"entrypoint": "manual", "outcome": "provider_error"})
        self.assert_private_signals(code)

    def test_outcome_counter_supports_failure_rate_comparison(self):
        provider = Provider()
        runner = self.runner(provider)
        for failure in (False, False, True, True):
            provider.error = ProviderError("TIMEOUT", "fixture-only-token") if failure else None
            run_id = runner.scheduled(self.job)
            runner.execute(run_id)

        rows = self.outcomes()
        self.assertEqual(len(rows), 4)
        rates = [
            sum(row["amount"] for row in window if row["labels"]["outcome"] != "success")
            / sum(row["amount"] for row in window)
            for window in (rows[:2], rows[2:])
        ]
        self.assertEqual(rates, [0, 1])
        self.assertEqual(len(provider.calls), 4)
        self.assertTrue(all(isinstance(row["time"], (float, int)) for row in rows))
        self.assert_private_signals("TIMEOUT")

    def test_unexpected_provider_exception_keeps_exception_and_queue(self):
        error = RuntimeError("private@example.test fixture-only-token")
        provider = Provider(error)
        runner = self.runner(provider)
        run_id = runner.manual(self.job)

        with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError) as raised:
            runner.execute(run_id)

        self.assertIs(raised.exception, error)
        self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [self.job])
        self.assertTrue((self.root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).exists())
        self.assertEqual(self.state(run_id)["failure_stage"], "send")
        self.assertEqual(self.state(run_id)["failure_kind"], "unexpected_error")
        self.assertEqual([row["labels"]["outcome"] for row in self.outcomes()], ["unexpected_error"])
        self.assert_private_signals()

    def test_queue_load_failure_keeps_exception_without_provider_call(self):
        provider = Provider()
        runner = self.runner(provider)
        run_id = runner.manual(self.job)
        path = self.root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")
        path.write_text("not-json-private@example.test")

        with self.assertRaises(json.JSONDecodeError):
            runner.execute(run_id)

        self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [])
        self.assertTrue(path.exists())
        self.assertEqual(self.state(run_id)["failure_stage"], "load")
        self.assertEqual(self.state(run_id)["entrypoint"], "unknown")
        self.assertEqual(self.outcomes()[0]["labels"]["outcome"], "unexpected_error")
        self.assert_private_signals()

    def test_queue_removal_failure_is_distinct_from_provider_success(self):
        provider = Provider()
        runner = self.runner(provider)
        run_id = runner.scheduled(self.job)
        error = PermissionError("private@example.test fixture-only-token")

        with patch.object(Path, "unlink", side_effect=error):
            with self.assertRaises(PermissionError) as raised:
                runner.execute(run_id)

        self.assertIs(raised.exception, error)
        self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [self.job])
        self.assertTrue((self.root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).exists())
        self.assertEqual(self.state(run_id)["failure_stage"], "acknowledge")
        self.assertEqual([row["labels"]["outcome"] for row in self.outcomes()], ["unexpected_error"])
        self.assert_private_signals()

    def test_unavailable_collector_preserves_success_and_failure_contracts(self):
        for error in (None, ProviderError("TIMEOUT", "fixture-only-token"), RuntimeError("fixture-only-token")):
            with self.subTest(error=type(error).__name__):
                provider = Provider(error)
                runner = self.runner(provider, Telemetry(self.root / "signals", available=False))
                run_id = runner.manual(self.job)

                if isinstance(error, RuntimeError):
                    with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError) as raised:
                        runner.execute(run_id)
                    self.assertIs(raised.exception, error)
                else:
                    result = runner.execute(run_id)
                    expected = {"run_id": run_id, "ok": error is None}
                    expected.update({"receipt": "receipt-12"} if error is None else {"code": "TIMEOUT"})
                    self.assertEqual(result, expected)

                self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [self.job])
                self.assertEqual(
                    (self.root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).exists(), isinstance(error, RuntimeError),
                )
        self.assertEqual(list((self.root / "signals").iterdir()), [])

    def test_each_collector_surface_can_fail_without_suppressing_the_others(self):
        for surface in ("record", "increment", "save_state"):
            with self.subTest(surface=surface):
                provider = Provider(ProviderError("TIMEOUT", "fixture-only-token"))
                runner = self.runner(provider)
                previous_outcomes = len(self.outcomes())

                with patch.object(self.telemetry, surface, side_effect=OSError("collector unavailable")):
                    run_id = runner.manual(self.job)
                    result = runner.execute(run_id)

                self.assertEqual(result, {"run_id": run_id, "ok": False, "code": "TIMEOUT"})
                self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [self.job])
                self.assertFalse((self.root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).exists())
                if surface != "record":
                    self.assertTrue(any(row["run_id"] == run_id for row in self.records("events.jsonl")))
                if surface != "save_state":
                    self.assertEqual(self.state(run_id)["status"], "failed")
                if surface != "increment":
                    self.assertEqual(len(self.outcomes()), previous_outcomes + 1)

    def test_legacy_and_unrecognized_entrypoints_have_bounded_unknown_label(self):
        runner = self.runner()
        for origin in (None, "private@example.test", ["fixture-only-token"]):
            with self.subTest(origin=origin):
                run_id = runner.manual(self.job)
                path = self.root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")
                message = json.loads(path.read_text())
                if origin is None:
                    del message["entrypoint"]
                else:
                    message["entrypoint"] = origin
                path.write_text(json.dumps(message))

                result = runner.execute(run_id)

                self.assertTrue(result["ok"])
                self.assertEqual(self.state(run_id)["entrypoint"], "unknown")
                self.assertEqual(self.outcomes()[-1]["labels"]["entrypoint"], "unknown")
        self.assert_private_signals()

    def test_enqueue_failure_is_reported_without_changing_exception(self):
        runner = self.runner()

        with self.assertRaises(TypeError):
            runner.manual({"not_json_serializable": object()})

        self.assertEqual(list((self.root / "queue").iterdir()), [])
        events = self.records("events.jsonl")
        self.assertEqual(events[-1]["failure_stage"], "enqueue")
        self.assertEqual(events[-1]["entrypoint"], "manual")
        self.assertEqual(self.records("metrics.jsonl")[-1]["metric"], "batch_enqueue_failures")
        self.assertEqual(self.outcomes(), [])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

and review produce recommendations; authorized implementation adds and verifies
the instrumentation. Work with the project's existing language and telemetry tools.

## Establish the diagnostic questions

Read the affected operations, entry points, asynchronous boundaries, failure paths,
and existing logs, metrics, traces, status surfaces and alerts. Identify who uses
the signals, where they can read them, and the relevant access, retention and cost
constraints. Reuse useful coverage before adding another producer or backend.

Choose concrete questions from the task and plausible failure modes: which run
failed, why a branch was taken, whether work is progressing, how often a dependency
fails, or where time is spent. Map each question to the smallest useful signal and
an observation that would answer it. Include success or recovery when needed to
distinguish failure from expected operation. A simple change need not acquire every
signal type, a dashboard, an alert or a new service.

`debug` owns investigating an observed failure; this skill owns durable diagnostic
coverage. `error-handling` owns caller-visible errors, retries and recovery policy.
An instrumentation change preserves results, exceptions, cancellation, effects and
retry ownership unless a behavior change is also authorized. During authorized
instrumentation, record a caught failure that would otherwise be silent with safe
classification and operation identity. Preserve what the caller receives; route
changes to that contract to `error-handling`.

## Instrument the deciding boundaries

Use established event names, levels, units and semantic conventions. Record
meaningful outcomes and decisions in structured fields, including the safe values
or classifications that explain them. Function entry/exit chatter rarely answers
an operational question. Give duplicate reports of one failure a clear owner rather than paging
at every layer.

| Signal | Use it to answer | Preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Structured log or event | What happened in this particular operation, and why? | Stable event name, time, operation/run identity, outcome and useful decision context |
| Metric | How much, how often, how slow, or how saturated? | Defined units, counted population, time window and bounded dimensions; distinguish attempts from logical operations |
| Trace | Where did an operation spend time across components? | The existing trace context, meaningful spans and links across synchronous and asynchronous boundaries |
| Health or status surface | Is a process alive, ready or making progress? | The specific state being measured, its scope and freshness; absence of errors alone is not evidence of health |

Create or validate correlation context at the trusted entry point and propagate it
through the affected calls, queues and workers. When several entry points share a
sink, record which entry point started the work alongside its run identity; a
correlation ID alone cannot establish that. Keep retries and child operations
associated without conflating separate executions. Treat incoming identifiers as
untrusted, bounded input and use the existing propagation format.

For metrics, use a bounded vocabulary such as operation, route template or outcome
class. Request IDs, user IDs, raw URLs and arbitrary error text do not belong in
metric dimensions. Histograms or an existing distribution measure support tail
latency questions; an average alone does not. Confirm what the instrument counts,
including retries, partial results and zero traffic, before deriving a rate.

Reuse existing tracing and auto-instrumentation; add manual spans where they answer
a missing question. Choose sampling and retention against diagnostic needs and
cost. Sampled traces cannot establish complete event counts or that an unrecorded
failure never happened. OpenTelemetry is an option, not a required migration.

## Keep diagnostic data safe and affordable

Allowlist fields before emission to logs, spans, metrics, persisted failures and
status responses. Raw exception messages, causes, stacks, URLs and payloads can
contain secrets or personal data even when the public error is generic. Preserve
useful classification and safe identifiers without copying unrestricted objects.
Apply the project's access and retention policy to every new diagnostic surface.

Bound payload size, label cardinality, event volume and buffer growth. Avoid
expensive serialization, blocking writes or per-iteration logging on hot paths;
aggregate, sample or use existing buffering when appropriate. Account for exporter
failure and backpressure so added telemetry does not unexpectedly fail or stall
the operation. Preserve an established mandatory audit contract, including its
failure policy, rather than silently making it best effort.

## Preserve evidence for unattended work

For background jobs, watchers or long-running processes, identify what remains
available after a crash or restart. Use the existing durable sink or state store;
add a failure record only where the diagnostic question needs one. Include safe
operation identity, phase, time, attempt and failure classification.

Scope state to the run or work item that produced it. Use the storage mechanism's
atomicity and concurrency controls so concurrent writers or a partial write do
not destroy evidence. Distinguish historical failure from current state: define
freshness and how success, recovery, restart or expiration updates it. An unrelated
successful job must not erase another job's failure.

Keep status reads cheap and free of business side effects. Distinguish liveness,
readiness and progress using the project's existing contract; a dependency outage
does not automatically justify declaring the process dead and restarting it.
Expose only the detail the intended reader is authorized to see.

## Add actionable alerts when needed

Use existing alert ownership, severity and delivery conventions. Choose conditions
that justify an action, usually user-visible errors, latency or delayed work; a
resource signal is useful when it predicts a concrete operational consequence.
Derive thresholds, duration and recovery conditions from service objectives,
observed behavior or an explicit project requirement. Identify the responder and
link the first useful query, mitigation or runbook. State how no traffic, stale
data and missing telemetry differ from recovery. Do not invent universal numbers
or delete existing alerts merely because they use another convention.

## Verify the signals at their destination

For design or review, inspect available evidence and state which checks remain
unrun. When execution is authorized, exercise the affected success and representative
failure paths in an isolated environment. Confirm that the intended trigger occurred, then
read the resulting events, metric series, traces or status at the consumer. Check
correlation across relevant entry points and boundaries, safe fields, expected
counts and units, and any new state lifecycle. A configured exporter or successful
test command alone does not prove that a signal arrived. Answer each diagnostic
question from the observed signals as a reader without the original context would.
If answering requires inspecting the implementation or rerunning the operation,
record the missing diagnostic evidence as a blind spot.

Use test collectors and notification sinks for failure injection and alert tests.
Production disruption, threshold changes or messages to real recipients need
authority from the active task; this skill grants none. Test delivery only through
the stages actually available and report unavailable destinations separately.
Missing or sampled-away data is unknown, not a zero error rate or verified health.

Verify that instrumentation preserves functional outcomes and relevant failure
behavior; exercise a telemetry outage when its new failure path can affect them.
Measure overhead under representative conditions when the changed path or budget
makes it material. Use available `verify` and project checks for execution evidence;
direct checks remain useful when that skill is unavailable. Remove only temporary
probes and fault controls owned by the task, preserving useful diagnostic evidence.

Report the questions covered, changes or findings, where and how to inspect each
signal, observed checks and remaining blind spots. Keep implementation, tested
delivery and production operation distinct. Return to the active caller for
remaining work; `ci-cd-automation` owns rollout gates and deployment recovery.
Publication or ongoing monitoring follows the user's existing scope.

For a requested check or update of this skill's sources, read
[references/upstream-updates.md](references/upstream-updates.md).

# Batch sender

The scheduler and manual operator enqueue work; another Runner instance executes
it after the producer has exited. A known ProviderError is returned as an outcome
and consumes the message. The external provider is called once per execution.
Other exceptions retain their existing behavior. This exercise has no live service.

telemetry.py is the existing local collector, not a mandatory audit trail. It
records exactly the fields supplied; it does not redact them. Its event, counter
and per-key state APIs write real files. New instrumentation can use these APIs.
The collector can be unavailable. The queue payload is private application state;
signals are read by support staff. Customer fields and provider diagnostics in the
fixtures are synthetic but represent confidential production data.

Public methods and result shapes are established contracts. No new backend,
package, deployment, notification channel or retry policy is requested.
Run the existing contract tests with python3 -m unittest -v. Add meaningful checks
for new instrumentation when needed.

## Reading the local signals

The queue now carries `entry_point` (`scheduled` or `manual`) with the generated
run ID. A fresh worker reads it from the queue. Missing or invalid origins are
reported as `unknown`; the worker does not infer an origin from the customer job.
Signals accept only 32-character lowercase hexadecimal run IDs. Other caller
identifiers receive a fresh diagnostic ID for that execution; their public result
and queue lookup stay unchanged, but they cannot be correlated across executions.

In the configured collector directory:

- `events.jsonl` preserves `batch.queued`, `batch.progress`, and
  `batch.execution_finished` events. Filter by `run_id`; use `execution_id` to
  separate repeat executions. The queued event identifies the producer. The first
  worker event uses `unknown` until it reads the queue.
- `run-<run_id>.json` is the atomic, most recently written state for that run.
  `phase` identifies the last observed boundary: `queued`, `queue_read`,
  `provider_send`, `queue_remove`, or `complete`. `time` is Unix seconds. A
  `queue_remove` event means the provider returned or raised a known ProviderError;
  its outcome records that result before queue consumption. An unexpected exception
  records its failing phase and is reraised unchanged. A later attempt replaces
  current state for that run; historical events remain. Other runs use other keys.
- `metrics.jsonl` contains `batch_execution_outcomes`, with amount 1 and unit
  executions. It counts each normally returning or exception-raising execution
  once, including repeat executions and queue-read failures, provided collection
  succeeds. Labels are bounded to `entry_point` (`scheduled`, `manual`, `unknown`)
  and `outcome` (`success`, `provider_error`, `unexpected_error`). It does not count
  unique runs or provider calls. For equal time windows, sum failure outcomes and
  divide by all outcomes to compare observed failure fractions; also compare raw
  counts and traffic. No completed executions means an undefined fraction.

Only the fields above and bounded `failure_class` values are emitted.
`TIMEOUT` maps to `provider_timeout`; other provider codes map to `provider_error`.
Unexpected exceptions map to `unexpected_error`. Jobs, receipts, provider messages,
raw codes, stacks, and customer fields are excluded. Public results are unchanged.

Each collector operation is independently best effort. A crash, collector outage,
or partial signal delivery can leave state stale or counters incomplete. `running`
means last observed progress, not proof of current liveness; absence of failures
is not proof of health. The state timestamp has no automatic expiry. Concurrent
executions of the same run share last-writer state, while events distinguish their
execution IDs. This does not add queue locking or change retry policy.

The existing collector writes synchronously and supplies no write deadline,
retention, access control, remote export, or alerts. Signals use its existing
directory and permissions. They grow with runs and executions; deployments must
apply their own retention and access policy. Tests verify local files only, not
remote delivery, filesystem crash durability, or production behavior.

import json
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from runner import ProviderError, Runner
from telemetry import Telemetry
from test_runner import Provider


HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
PRIVATE = "fixture-only-token; private@example.test"
JOB = {"kind": "invoice", "email": "private@example.test", "credential": "fixture-only-token"}


def read_lines(root, name):
    path = root / name
    return [json.loads(line) for line in path.read_text().splitlines()] if path.exists() else []


class ObservabilityTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_origins_and_outcomes_survive_producer_process_exit(self):
        for entry_point in ("scheduled", "manual"):
            for fails in (False, True):
                with self.subTest(entry_point=entry_point, fails=fails), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=HERE) as folder:
                    root = Path(folder)
                    producer = subprocess.run(
                        [sys.executable, "-c", "\n".join([
                            "import json, sys",
                            "from pathlib import Path",
                            "from runner import Runner",
                            "from telemetry import Telemetry",
                            "root = Path(sys.argv[1])",
                            "runner = Runner(root / 'queue', None, Telemetry(root / 'signals'))",
                            "print(getattr(runner, sys.argv[2])(json.loads(sys.argv[3])))",
                        ]), str(root), entry_point, json.dumps(JOB)],
                        cwd=HERE, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True,
                    )
                    run_id = producer.stdout.strip()
                    queued = json.loads((root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).read_text())
                    self.assertEqual(queued["entry_point"], entry_point)
                    provider = Provider(ProviderError("TIMEOUT", PRIVATE) if fails else None)
                    worker = Runner(root / "queue", provider, Telemetry(root / "signals"))

                    result = worker.execute(run_id)

                    expected = {"run_id": run_id, "ok": not fails}
                    expected.update({"code": "TIMEOUT"} if fails else {"receipt": "receipt-12"})
                    self.assertEqual(result, expected)
                    self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [JOB])
                    self.assertFalse((root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).exists())
                    events = read_lines(root / "signals", "events.jsonl")
                    self.assertEqual([event["phase"] for event in events], [
                        "queued", "queue_read", "provider_send", "queue_remove", "complete",
                    ])
                    self.assertEqual({event["run_id"] for event in events}, {run_id})
                    self.assertEqual(events[0]["entry_point"], entry_point)
                    self.assertEqual(events[1]["entry_point"], "unknown")
                    self.assertEqual({event["entry_point"] for event in events[2:]}, {entry_point})
                    self.assertEqual(len({event["execution_id"] for event in events[1:]}), 1)
                    state = json.loads((root / "signals" / ("run-" + run_id + ".json")).read_text())
                    self.assertEqual(state["phase"], "complete")
                    self.assertEqual(state["outcome"], "provider_error" if fails else "success")
                    self.assertEqual(state["entry_point"], entry_point)
                    self.assertEqual(state["execution_id"], events[-1]["execution_id"])
                    self.assertIsInstance(state["time"], (float, int))
                    if fails:
                        self.assertEqual(state["failure_class"], "provider_timeout")
                    metrics = read_lines(root / "signals", "metrics.jsonl")
                    self.assertEqual(len(metrics), 1)
                    self.assertEqual(metrics[0]["metric"], "batch_execution_outcomes")
                    self.assertEqual(metrics[0]["amount"], 1)
                    self.assertEqual(metrics[0]["labels"], {
                        "entry_point": entry_point,
                        "outcome": "provider_error" if fails else "success",
                    })
                    for signal in events + [state]:
                        self.assertLessEqual(set(signal), {
                            "time", "event", "run_id", "entry_point", "execution_id",
                            "phase", "outcome", "failure_class",
                        })
                    self.assert_safe_signals(root / "signals")

    def assert_safe_signals(self, signals):
        emitted = "\n".join(path.read_text() for path in signals.iterdir())
        for private in ("fixture-only-token", "private@example.test", "receipt-12", "invoice"):
            self.assertNotIn(private, emitted)

    def test_arbitrary_provider_code_and_receipt_stay_in_public_result_only(self):
        class PrivateReceiptProvider(Provider):
            def send(self, job):
                super().send(job)
                return PRIVATE

        for provider in (Provider(ProviderError(PRIVATE, PRIVATE)), PrivateReceiptProvider()):
            with self.subTest(provider=type(provider).__name__), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=HERE) as folder:
                root = Path(folder)
                runner = Runner(root / "queue", provider, Telemetry(root / "signals"))
                run_id = runner.manual(JOB)

                result = runner.execute(run_id)

                self.assertEqual(result.get("code", result.get("receipt")), PRIVATE)
                self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [JOB])
                self.assert_safe_signals(root / "signals")
                if not result["ok"]:
                    terminal = read_lines(root / "signals", "events.jsonl")[-1]
                    self.assertEqual(terminal["failure_class"], "provider_error")

    def test_unrelated_success_preserves_failed_run_state(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=HERE) as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            telemetry = Telemetry(root / "signals")
            failure = Runner(root / "queue", Provider(ProviderError("TIMEOUT", PRIVATE)), telemetry)
            failed_id = failure.scheduled(JOB)
            failure.execute(failed_id)
            failed_path = root / "signals" / ("run-" + failed_id + ".json")
            original_failure = failed_path.read_bytes()
            success = Runner(root / "queue", Provider(), telemetry)
            successful_id = success.manual(JOB)

            success.execute(successful_id)

            self.assertEqual(failed_path.read_bytes(), original_failure)
            self.assertNotEqual(failed_id, successful_id)
            self.assertEqual(len(read_lines(root / "signals", "metrics.jsonl")), 2)

    def test_unexpected_error_is_reraised_and_retry_has_new_execution_id(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=HERE) as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            error = RuntimeError(PRIVATE)
            provider = Provider(error)
            runner = Runner(root / "queue", provider, Telemetry(root / "signals"))
            run_id = runner.manual(JOB)

            with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError) as raised:
                runner.execute(run_id)

            self.assertIs(raised.exception, error)
            self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [JOB])
            self.assertTrue((root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).exists())
            first_state = json.loads((root / "signals" / ("run-" + run_id + ".json")).read_text())
            self.assertEqual(first_state["phase"], "provider_send")
            self.assertEqual(first_state["outcome"], "unexpected_error")
            replacement_provider = Provider()
            replacement = Runner(root / "queue", replacement_provider, Telemetry(root / "signals"))

            self.assertTrue(replacement.execute(run_id)["ok"])

            self.assertEqual(replacement_provider.calls, [JOB])
            state = json.loads((root / "signals" / ("run-" + run_id + ".json")).read_text())
            self.assertNotEqual(state["execution_id"], first_state["execution_id"])
            self.assertEqual(state["outcome"], "success")
            terminal = [event for event in read_lines(root / "signals", "events.jsonl")
                        if event["event"] == "batch.execution_finished"]
            self.assertEqual([event["outcome"] for event in terminal], ["unexpected_error", "success"])
            metrics = read_lines(root / "signals", "metrics.jsonl")
            self.assertEqual([metric["labels"]["outcome"] for metric in metrics], ["unexpected_error", "success"])
            self.assert_safe_signals(root / "signals")

    def test_collector_outage_preserves_success_known_failure_and_unexpected_error(self):
        for error in (None, ProviderError("TIMEOUT", PRIVATE), RuntimeError(PRIVATE)):
            with self.subTest(error=type(error).__name__), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=HERE) as folder:
                root = Path(folder)
                provider = Provider(error)
                runner = Runner(root / "queue", provider, Telemetry(root / "signals", available=False))
                run_id = runner.scheduled(JOB)

                if isinstance(error, RuntimeError):
                    with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError) as raised:
                        runner.execute(run_id)
                    self.assertIs(raised.exception, error)
                else:
                    result = runner.execute(run_id)
                    expected = {"run_id": run_id, "ok": error is None}
                    expected.update({"code": "TIMEOUT"} if error else {"receipt": "receipt-12"})
                    self.assertEqual(result, expected)

                self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [JOB])
                self.assertEqual((root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).exists(), isinstance(error, RuntimeError))
                self.assertEqual(list((root / "signals").iterdir()), [])

    def test_event_sink_failure_does_not_prevent_state_or_metric_delivery(self):
        class EventOutage(Telemetry):
            def record(self, event, **fields):
                raise OSError("event sink unavailable")

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=HERE) as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            provider = Provider()
            runner = Runner(root / "queue", provider, EventOutage(root / "signals"))
            run_id = runner.manual(JOB)

            self.assertTrue(runner.execute(run_id)["ok"])

            self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [JOB])
            self.assertFalse((root / "signals" / "events.jsonl").exists())
            self.assertEqual(len(read_lines(root / "signals", "metrics.jsonl")), 1)
            state = json.loads((root / "signals" / ("run-" + run_id + ".json")).read_text())
            self.assertEqual(state["phase"], "complete")

    def test_invalid_or_legacy_origin_is_bounded_and_job_is_unchanged(self):
        for origin in (None, PRIVATE, [PRIVATE], {"secret": PRIVATE}):
            with self.subTest(origin=type(origin).__name__), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=HERE) as folder:
                root = Path(folder)
                provider = Provider()
                runner = Runner(root / "queue", provider, Telemetry(root / "signals"))
                run_id = "a" * 32
                message = {"run_id": PRIVATE, "job": JOB}
                if origin is not None:
                    message["entry_point"] = origin
                (root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).write_text(json.dumps(message))

                result = runner.execute(run_id)

                self.assertTrue(result["ok"])
                self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [JOB])
                events = read_lines(root / "signals", "events.jsonl")
                self.assertEqual({event["entry_point"] for event in events}, {"unknown"})
                self.assertEqual({event["run_id"] for event in events}, {run_id})
                self.assert_safe_signals(root / "signals")

    def test_untrusted_run_id_is_not_emitted_or_used_as_state_key(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=HERE) as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            provider = Provider()
            runner = Runner(root / "queue", provider, Telemetry(root / "signals"))
            run_id = "private@example.test"
            (root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).write_text(json.dumps({"job": JOB}))

            result = runner.execute(run_id)

            self.assertEqual(result["run_id"], run_id)
            self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [JOB])
            events = read_lines(root / "signals", "events.jsonl")
            safe_id = events[0]["run_id"]
            self.assertRegex(safe_id, r"^[0-9a-f]{32}$")
            self.assertEqual({event["run_id"] for event in events}, {safe_id})
            self.assertTrue((root / "signals" / ("run-" + safe_id + ".json")).exists())
            self.assert_safe_signals(root / "signals")

    def test_queue_read_failures_are_visible_without_provider_calls(self):
        for payload, error_type in ((None, FileNotFoundError), ("{", json.JSONDecodeError), ("{}", KeyError)):
            with self.subTest(error=error_type.__name__), tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=HERE) as folder:
                root = Path(folder)
                provider = Provider()
                runner = Runner(root / "queue", provider, Telemetry(root / "signals"))
                run_id = "b" * 32
                path = root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")
                if payload is not None:
                    path.write_text(payload)

                with self.assertRaises(error_type):
                    runner.execute(run_id)

                self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [])
                self.assertEqual(path.exists(), payload is not None)
                state = json.loads((root / "signals" / ("run-" + run_id + ".json")).read_text())
                self.assertEqual((state["phase"], state["outcome"]), ("queue_read", "unexpected_error"))
                self.assertEqual(read_lines(root / "signals", "metrics.jsonl")[0]["labels"], {
                    "entry_point": "unknown", "outcome": "unexpected_error",
                })

    def test_queue_removal_error_keeps_provider_at_one_call(self):
        class QueueCollisionProvider(Provider):
            def send(self, job):
                receipt = super().send(job)
                queue_path.unlink()
                queue_path.mkdir()
                return receipt

        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=HERE) as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            provider = QueueCollisionProvider()
            runner = Runner(root / "queue", provider, Telemetry(root / "signals"))
            run_id = runner.manual(JOB)
            queue_path = root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")

            with self.assertRaises(OSError):
                runner.execute(run_id)

            self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [JOB])
            state = json.loads((root / "signals" / ("run-" + run_id + ".json")).read_text())
            self.assertEqual((state["phase"], state["outcome"]), ("queue_remove", "unexpected_error"))
            self.assertEqual(len(read_lines(root / "signals", "metrics.jsonl")), 1)

    def test_abrupt_worker_exit_leaves_last_progress_without_a_false_outcome(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=HERE) as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            producer = Runner(root / "queue", None, Telemetry(root / "signals"))
            run_id = producer.scheduled(JOB)

            worker = subprocess.run(
                [sys.executable, "-c", "\n".join([
                    "import os, sys",
                    "from pathlib import Path",
                    "from runner import Runner",
                    "from telemetry import Telemetry",
                    "class ExitingProvider:",
                    "    def send(self, job):",
                    "        os._exit(23)",
                    "root = Path(sys.argv[1])",
                    "Runner(root / 'queue', ExitingProvider(), Telemetry(root / 'signals')).execute(sys.argv[2])",
                ]), str(root), run_id],
                cwd=HERE, capture_output=True, text=True,
            )

            self.assertEqual(worker.returncode, 23, worker.stderr)
            self.assertTrue((root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).exists())
            state = json.loads((root / "signals" / ("run-" + run_id + ".json")).read_text())
            self.assertEqual((state["phase"], state["outcome"]), ("provider_send", "running"))
            self.assertEqual(state["entry_point"], "scheduled")
            self.assertEqual(read_lines(root / "signals", "metrics.jsonl"), [])
            self.assertFalse(any(event["event"] == "batch.execution_finished"
                                 for event in read_lines(root / "signals", "events.jsonl")))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from runner import ProviderError, Runner
from telemetry import Telemetry


class Provider:
    def __init__(self, error=None):
        self.error = error
        self.calls = []

    def send(self, job):
        self.calls.append(job)
        if self.error:
            raise self.error
        return "receipt-12"


class ContractTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_success_after_fresh_worker_start(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            root = Path(folder)
            provider = Provider()
            telemetry = Telemetry(root / "signals")
            producer = Runner(root / "queue", provider, telemetry)
            job = {"kind": "invoice", "email": "private@example.test", "credential": "fixture-only-token"}
            run_id = producer.scheduled(job)
            consumer = Runner(root / "queue", provider, telemetry)

            result = consumer.execute(run_id)

            self.assertEqual(result, {"run_id": run_id, "ok": True, "receipt": "receipt-12"})
            self.assertEqual(provider.calls, [job])
            self.assertFalse((root / "queue" / (run_id + ".json")).exists())

    def test_provider_failure_keeps_result_and_at_most_once_attempt(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            root = Path(folder)

import collections
import hashlib
import json
import re
import shutil
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path

root = Path.cwd()
package = root / 'observability'
manifest = json.loads((root / '.tmp/observability/review-v2/manifest.json').read_text())
for path, digest in manifest.items():
    assert hashlib.sha256((root / path).read_bytes()).hexdigest() == digest, path
origin = tomllib.loads((package / 'origin.txt').read_text())
assert len(origin['sources']) == 2
notice = (package / 'THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt').read_text()
for donor in ('addy', 'gsd'):
    license_text = (root / '.tmp/observability/sources' / donor / 'LICENSE').read_text()
    assert license_text in notice
copy = root / '.tmp/observability/relocated-package/observability'
shutil.copytree(package, copy, dirs_exist_ok=True)
for path in copy.rglob('*.md'):
    assert not path.is_symlink()
    content = path.read_text()
    assert '/Users/' not in content and '.tmp/' not in content
    for target in re.findall(r'\]\(([^)]+)\)', content):
        if not target.startswith(('https:', 'http:', '#')):
            resolved = (path.parent / target.split('#')[0]).resolve()
            assert resolved.is_relative_to(copy.resolve()) and resolved.is_file(), target

atlas_root = root / 'reports/skill-atlas'
raw = (atlas_root / 'sources.json').read_text()
atlas = json.loads(raw)
assert (atlas_root / 'catalog.js').read_text() == 'window.SKILL_ATLAS = ' + raw.rstrip() + ';\n'
inventory = atlas['repositoryInventory']['skills']
assert len({entry['name'] for entry in inventory}) == len(inventory)
entry = next(item for item in inventory if item['name'] == 'observability')
assert entry['sha256'] == manifest['observability/SKILL.md']
progress = atlas['sourceProgress']
assert dict(collections.Counter(item['status'] for item in progress['skills'].values())) == progress['counts']
for key in ('Addy Osmani/observability-and-instrumentation', 'GSD/observability'):
    entry = progress['skills'][key]
    assert entry['status'] == 'ready' and entry['owners'] == ['observability']
    evidence = entry['evidence'][0]
    path = root / evidence['path']
    assert hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() == evidence['sha256']
    source = next(source for source in origin['sources'] if source['id'] == evidence['sourceId'])
    assert evidence['baselineCommit'] == source['baseline_commit']
    assert evidence['reviewedThrough'] == source['reviewed_through']
    assert path.read_text().splitlines()[evidence['line'] - 1] == 'id = "' + source['id'] + '"'

before = json.loads((root / '.tmp/observability/atlas-before.json').read_text())
for key, old in before.items():
    if key not in {'authorReview', 'repositoryInventory', 'sourceProgress'}:
        assert atlas[key] == old, 'Unrelated atlas block changed: ' + key
assert atlas['authorReview']['skills'] == before['authorReview']['skills']
for key, old in before['sourceProgress']['skills'].items():
    if key != 'Addy Osmani/observability-and-instrumentation':
        assert progress['skills'][key] == old, key
assert [item for item in inventory if item['name'] != 'observability'] == before['repositoryInventory']['skills']
html = (atlas_root / 'index.html').read_text()
for script in ('app.js', 'catalog.js'):
    digest = hashlib.sha256((atlas_root / script).read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:12]
    assert script + '?v=' + digest in html
assert 'id="observability"' in html and 'href="#observability"' in html
assert '### observability\n' in (root / 'README.md').read_text()
registry = json.loads((root / 'skills.sh.json').read_text())
assert 'observability' in [skill for group in registry['groupings'] for skill in group['skills']]
